title: Sunday garage
topic: A friend adds up a Sunday parking tab across a free-after-6 cutoff
blurb: First hour, extra half-hours, a 6 PM cutoff, and a crisp $11.50 kiosk bill.
prompt: A friend texted this walking out of the matinee. Tap a line if the parking math is off, or call it clean.

segments.label: The sign
segments.text: Downtown garage is $4 for the first hour, $2.50 for each extra half hour, and Sundays are free after 6 PM.

segments.label: The stay
segments.text: Pulled in at 3:30 PM Sunday for the movie and drove out at 7:15 PM.

segments.label: The tab
segments.text: Paid $11.50 at the kiosk — first hour took me to 4:30, three half-hours got me to 6:00, and the last 75 minutes were free.

segments.label: The win
segments.text: Way cheaper than the $18 flat lot across the street.

conclusion: $4 for 3:30–4:30 plus $7.50 for 4:30–6:00 and free after 6:00 comes out to $11.50.

diagnosis: Garages that say 'free after 6 PM' only apply if you enter after 6 PM, not if your ticket started earlier.
$2.50 per half hour is $5 an hour, so the first hour is cheaper and can't be added directly to half-hour blocks.
Sunday rates usually replace the hourly sign with a flat weekend maximum instead of mixing both.
Listing an hour rate and a half-hour rate without mentioning the grace period makes the 7:15 exit billable.
fix: Count the full 3 hours 45 minutes at hourly rates since you entered before 6 PM.
Convert the first hour to two half-hours ($5) before summing the stay.
Check if the garage charges a Sunday flat fee before assuming free after 6.
Verify whether the 15 minutes past 7:00 triggers an extra half-hour charge.

diagnosis: From 3:30 PM to 7:15 PM is 4 hours and 15 minutes, not 3 hours and 45 minutes.
Driving out at 7:15 PM means you stayed past 7:00, so the kiosk rounds up to four full hours.
Entering at 3:30 PM puts the half-hour boundaries on :00 and :30, so 7:15 adds an extra block.
Leaving at 7:15 PM is 1 hour 15 minutes after 6:00 — that's 65 minutes, not 75.
fix: Recount 3:30 to 7:15 as 4 hours 15 minutes before pricing the ticket.
Round the 7:15 exit up to 7:30 since garages bill partial half-hours in full.
Change the free window from 75 minutes to 65 minutes.
Exit before 7:00 PM next time to avoid crossing into a fourth paid hour.

diagnosis: Three half-hours at $2.50 is $6.50, not $7.50, so the kiosk should have charged $10.50.
From 4:30 to 6:00 is four half-hour blocks (4:30, 5:00, 5:30, 6:00), which makes the bill $14.00.
Staying until 7:15 PM adds three more half-hours after 6:00, bringing the real tab to $19.00.
From 3:30 to 6:00 is 2.5 hours — five half-hours at $2.50 is $12.50, not $11.50.
fix: Fix the arithmetic: $4.00 plus 3 × $2.50 is $10.50, not $11.50.
Bill all 3 hours 45 minutes straight through since entry was before 6:00 PM ($19.00).
Charge all 2.5 hours at $2.50 per half-hour to get $12.50.

diagnosis: If the full 3 hours 45 minutes were billed ($19.00), the $18 flat lot across the street was actually $1 cheaper.
Saving $6.50 only holds if you didn't have to walk farther or wait at the kiosk.
At $14.00 for four half-hours, the savings over the $18 lot is barely $4, not 'way cheaper'.
The flat lot across the street is probably also free on Sundays after 6 PM.
fix: Re-check the kiosk receipt — if you paid $19, take the $18 flat lot next time.
Check the flat lot's Sunday evening rate before calling the garage cheaper.
Note that you only saved $5.50 once the 2.5 hours are priced at $12.50.

Way cheaper than the $18 flat lot across the street.
clean_conclusion: Every block checks out: 3:30–4:30 is $4, 4:30–6:00 is three half-hours ($7.50), and 6:00–7:15 (75 minutes) is free on Sunday — $11.50 exact.
